outcome: Give describe_dataset a per-column profile, non-null and distinct counts with the range of numeric and temporal columns, so an agent sees repetition and gaps without an exploratory query.
criteria: describe_dataset reports for every column its non-null count and distinct count, and for numeric and temporal columns its minimum and maximum, computed in one scan of the current version; profile=false leaves them out.
The analytics engine protocol gains the profiling method, the DuckDB engine implements it, and a dataset with no physical version or beyond a column bound is described without a profile and says so.
Tests on the example orders data and a CSV with blanks cover the counts, the ranges, the opt-out and the MCP tool, and the full suite including the boundary tests passes.
The tool description and the README state the profile, and a pull request against Intentum main states the behaviour, tradeoffs and limitations.

note: profile_columns on the engine protocol and DuckDB: COUNT, COUNT(DISTINCT) per column and MIN/MAX for numeric and temporal columns in one scan. describe_dataset adds them to each schema entry with a profile sentence; profile=false leaves them out; beyond PROFILE_COLUMN_BOUND (300) columns or without a physical version the profile is skipped and says so. 4 new tests fail without the change; 406 passed. The PR is opened after this commit.
